production_source_comparison.interpretation: All 286 runtime/build paths match the tested cloud commit. Eight user extensions are retained; post-build documentation and original OC routing/selector research are separately recorded, not counted as part of cloud production verification.

limits: No real hardware setting, PBO effect or stability measurement has been verified.
Only Shimada family 1Ah/model 08h at PCI 1022:153a/BDF 0 is admitted for the new setting API.

Mode verification confirms only capability bit zero. Frequency confirms firmware acknowledgement only, never actual frequency or physical mapping. No automatic retries, rollback, MP1 fallback, VID or scalar reset.
Fmax still has acknowledgement only. Rails has only an offline bounded encoding preview; physical targets and its two-command transaction remain unverified.
Original dynamic-memory and EC dynamic-EDC paths remain research-only. Their original Applied/return behavior is not proof of firmware acceptance or effective hardware changes.
Per-core/CCD PM telemetry layout remains unresolved. Other AMD profiles, native PM transport, Intel server controls and board-specific settings remain incomplete.
EL7 means Oracle Linux 7.9 x86_64. Windows/macOS validate the portable core, not a full application port.
QEMU verifies module integration only; Secure Boot and actual register settings were not tested.

visual_review.method: Eight original PNGs opened with view_image and visually reviewed
observations: Mode success shows requested Enabled, firmware accepted, Enabled mode readback, Mode bit matches and complete before/after capability words.
Discarded-mode setting shows firmware accepted but Disabled readback, Not verified, and a failure status; no false success.
Single-core example clearly states Firmware CCD 15 / core 7 and physical mapping unverified; all-core example states All cores and clears/disables the individual selectors.
Both frequency examples show requested 5000 MHz, response 1 and unavailable/not verified current-frequency readback. They do not label requested MHz as measured MHz.
Requested manual OC mode is a separate desired-mode control, not a current-mode indicator; frequency operations use the fresh capability bit and do not apply that separate control.
New controls, result rows and full status text fit the 1300x1200 fixture viewport. Some pre-existing action labels use ellipsis; this is not whole-application visual acceptance.
limitations: Synthetic fixtures only; no real firmware setting, physical mapping or measured frequency.
The remaining 1312 desktop PNGs were archived but not individually viewed in this batch.

original_replay.scope: Original function instructions with original bounded constants. SMU writes, MP1, family predicates, locks and timing are synthetic boundaries; no firmware, PCI or Qt code executes.

observations: Original OC mode uses BIOS 24/25 with arg0=1, or Phoenix/GPT MP1 17/18. Original all-frequency uses BIOS 26 or MP1 19. These IDs/args are not the new RSMU protocol.

Modern single-core helper divides a flat target by eight but adjusts it using remainder modulo seven. Of 128 indices, 17 slow and 19 fast encodings differ from linear eight-core groups. Fast indices 0 and 7 select encoded CCD 15.
Original per-CCD helpers send eight core-index requests even with every synthetic SMU boundary returning FE. The loop is not evidence that all eight physical cores exist or succeeded.
Fast helpers write only argument zero and command; the normal helpers clear five other arguments. New RSMU initializes all six.

Original per-core frequency masks to 20 bits, accepting zero and wrapping negative/overflow inputs. Flat core 128 and CCD 16 alias lower targets. New API validates explicit CCD/core/MHz before any I/O.
Original Wr_ocvid clamps input to 700..2400 and Shimada uses floor((mV-245)/5), BIOS 28. This does not establish dual-rail RSMU 61 semantics.

REA UI apply shows implicit enableocmode, default 1250 mV and then per-CCD writes; Applied feedback is not firmware acceptance. Its two-rail call loses arguments in pseudocode and is not used as protocol evidence.
Pinned public Shimada table defines RSMU 5D/5E/5F/60. Public mode code uses zero argument and additionally resets scalar on disable. The new implementation omits that extra setting.

Mode verification checks only capability bit zero and retains full before/after words. Frequency remains acknowledgement-only, with no inferred physical target, current frequency or hardware verification.
PM per-core/CCD layouts, rails, native PM transport, dynamic memory/EC controls and other-platform writes remain unresolved.

local_user_port_tests.environment: Windows without a C++ compiler or Linux runtime; workspace TEMP used. Compiler/Linux cases were exercised by cloud workflows.

post_build_research.scope: Original OC instructions with synthetic SMU/MP1 boundaries; locally executed after the cloud production commit. Not a runtime component or actual firmware/physical-target validation.
